text:
Situation: FDA first posted the hydromorphone hydrochloride injection shortage on 2017-10-31 and it remains Current as of 2026-10-21. The posting lists Fresenius Kabi USA LLC, Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA Inc., Hospira Inc. (a Pfizer Company), and Teva Pharmaceuticals USA Inc. as affected companies. Corvale East holds 2.8 days of 2 mg/mL 20 mL vials; Corvale General holds 21.3 days of the same strength and size. Other concentrations at both sites have 13.8 to 29.1 days on hand.

Why (FDA record): FDA inspection 976095 at Hospira Inc. (FEI 1925262) ended 2016-06-08 and was classified OAI, 510 days before the shortage posting. A Warning Letter was issued to Hospira Inc. (FEI 1925262) on 2017-02-14, 259 days before the posting. FDA inspection 1031233 at Hospira Inc. (FEI 1925262) ended 2017-10-27 and was classified VAI, 4 days before the posting.

Our position: Corvale East is critically low on the 2 mg/mL 20 mL vial. Corvale General can spare inventory while retaining a two‑week supply. Alternate concentrations from Hikma and Hospira are approved for use with pharmacist verification.

Recommended actions:
1. Transfer 139 vials of 2 mg/mL 20 mL from Corvale General to Corvale East — requires pharmacy director approval and a DEA Form 222 or CSOS order (Schedule II).
2. Use Hikma 2 mg/mL alternate concentration or vial size — requires pharmacist verification; approved by Sam Rivera, MD on 2025-10-13.
3. Use Hospira 1 mg/mL alternate concentration or vial size — requires pharmacist verification; approved by Sam Rivera, MD on 2026-06-05; FDA lists this product Current (posted 2017-10-31).

Not recommended: No additional actions at this time.
